public_rationale: The February 3, 2026 International AI Safety Report describes limitations in technical safeguards and institutional risk management, but does not test whether policy alone can control agent harms [e1]. Lu and Bengio's September 9 proposal combines technical supervision, system controls and governance; it does not demonstrate their effectiveness or necessity [e2]. Neither source establishes the conditional absence of effective new technical approaches or a sustained policy-only outcome that would settle the forecast [e1, e2].
limitations: The claim supplies no deadline or measurable threshold for adequate safety.
Safeguard limitations and proposed remedies do not establish that policy alone must fail [e1, e2].
The packet contains no independently verified policy-only regime meeting the early-resolution rule [e1, e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Without new research approaches we will be in deep trouble, and policy alone will not make AI safe.
conditions: if we don't have new research approaches

statement.excerpt: And in fact, I think if we don’t have the new research approaches, like what Joshua is trying to do, for example, and I think we need many such approaches, then I think we were in deep trouble, and the policy alone will not get us there.

from_speaker: if we don’t have the new research approaches
like what Joshua is trying to do
the policy alone will not get us there
our_interpretation: I read the claim as saying that policy measures cannot reliably control the harmful actions of broadly capable AI agents without materially different technical approaches.
Policy includes enforceable restrictions and oversight, not merely voluntary promises.
The antecedent concerns the absence of effective new approaches during the relevant future period. The existence of research proposals does not establish whether that antecedent will hold.
No deadline or measurable standard for adequate safety is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: With the absence of effective new technical approaches established, decisive evidence shows that policy measures alone cannot reliably control the identified agent harms. Individual failures of particular policies are insufficient to establish this necessity.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Policy measures alone demonstrably achieve sustained, reliable control of the identified agent harms, without relying on materially new technical approaches.

evidence.locator: Layering multiple approaches offers more robust risk management
evidence.explanation: The report describes limitations of technical and institutional safeguards. It does not test whether policy alone could control agent harms under the forecast's antecedent.

evidence.excerpt: AI safety failures often arise across multiple layers.
evidence.explanation: Lu and Bengio propose combining technical supervision, system controls and governance. This establishes a research proposal, not the absence of effective new approaches or the impossibility of policy-only control.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A documented policy-only regime achieving sustained, independently verified control of specified agent harms without materially new technical approaches would contradict the forecast. Support would require establishing the absence of effective new approaches and showing that policy alone cannot reliably control those harms, beyond isolated implementation failures.
